proposals.before: She married Emperor Xuan and bore by concubines Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an; afterward she bore the Grand Ancestor.
proposals.after: She married Emperor Xuan; Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an were secondary-born (by concubines); afterward she bore the Grand Ancestor.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 庶生 marks Daodu and Daosheng as born of concubines, not borne by the empress; the literal wrongly makes her their mother.

proposals.before: She called Xiao Daocheng by his childhood name Doujiang and said, "It must be you."
proposals.after: She called the Grand Ancestor by his childhood name and said, "It must be you."
proposals.reason: The Chinese only has 小字 without giving the name Doujiang; the idiomatic invents a childhood name not in the source unit.

proposals.before: Her father Chen Zhao was made household minister with the purple-gold seal and posthumously titled Marquis Jing.
proposals.after: Her maternal grandfather Zhao was made household minister with the purple-gold seal and posthumously titled Marquis Jing.
proposals.reason: This unit's Chinese says 外祖父 (maternal grandfather), not father; the idiomatic contradicts the unit Chinese (though s0011 calls 肇之 father).

decisions.reason: In 嫁于宣帝，庶生衡陽元王道度、始安貞王道生，后生太祖, 庶生 marks Daodu and Daosheng as secondary-born (of concubines), while only 后生太祖 attributes maternity to the empress. The original literal's 'bore by concubines' wrongly makes her their mother; the proposed wording restores that distinction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 庶生衡陽元王道度、始安貞王道生，后生太祖

decisions.reason: 呼太祖小字曰 records only that she addressed him by childhood name; the graph 小字 does not supply the syllables Doujiang. Removing the invented childhood name aligns the idiomatic with the Chinese and with the existing literal.

decisions.after: His maternal grandfather Chen Zhaozhi was made household minister with the purple-gold seal and posthumously titled Marquis Jing.
decisions.reason: The emperor is the implicit possessor in 外祖父肇之, so this is his maternal grandfather; 肇之 is the man's full given name Zhaozhi, not Zhao. The revision preserves the Chen surname supplied by the preceding genealogy and corrects both the relationship and name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 贈外祖父肇之金紫光祿大夫，諡曰敬侯

claimRetractions.reason: Accepting r0002 shows the childhood name Doujiang was invented by the bad idiomatic; s0018 only has 小字 and supplies no such name form.
